title: Ratelimit enforcement race: admission controller vs cache invalidator causes multi-region 429 loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted and Dedicated customers, plus one Private deployment customer) experienced repeated 429s across regions after a routine rollout of a rate-limiting change. The surface failure looked like quota exhaustion followed by opaque downstream 429s and client-side retries that amplified load.

Impact: Intermittent but sustained 429s for 4 customers, highest impact for two Dedicated tenants with high request fan-out. Total incident window ~3.5 hours; automated fallback to lower-tier model reduced but did not eliminate errors for affected tenants.

Root cause (initial analysis): During the rollout we deployed a change that adjusted per-tenant admission ordering to prefer local token-bucket tokens before consulting the shared prefix cache. A separate async cache invalidator job was introduced to proactively evict prefix/KV entries on config change. Under a narrow timing window across regions the admission controller would see a stale local allowance while the cache invalidator simultaneously removed a shared lease; this led to a race where admission granted tokens that weren't actually reserved system-wide. The reconciliation path attempted to re-bind tokens and, on failure, returned a 429 that the proxy translated into an opaque 429 loop. Retries from clients (and our internal retry policy) amplified the effect into a multi-region fatigue state.

Why this manifested across Hosted/Dedicated/Private: Dedicated and Private deployments had differing cache TTLs and invalidation batching (to reduce control-plane load). The mismatch in invalidation granularity caused the same race to appear with higher probability on Dedicated nodes and the on-prem Private customer (where invalidation batches were longer). Hosted tenants were partially protected by a more aggressive fallback policy but some hosted customers with heavy fan-out hit the same edge.

Short-term mitigation performed: 1) Rolled back the admission ordering change on staging-to-prod canary nodes within 20 minutes of detection. 2) Disabled async cache invalidator batching for regions showing high desync. 3) Applied emergency proxy translation fallback to return a 503 with precise rate-metrics for affected tenants to prevent retry amplification. 4) Contacted impacted customers with status updates and temporary quota soft-locks while we repaired state.

Evidence / artifacts: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rl/ratelimit-incident-47955 (latency/429 traces).
Runbook used: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/Rate+Limit+Incidents
Customer escalation thread (redacted): https://gmail.redwood.company/threads/esc-47955
Preliminary PR for rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8643
